clue.text: Sound advice to climber enabling him to pull strings

definitions.text: Sound advice to climber enabling him to pull strings

parts.words: Sound advice to climber enabling him to pull strings
parts.note: said aloud, the answer is the warning 'don't lose your footing' a mountaineer needs, and it also names a loop that comes free when a cord is tugged

explanation.surface: A mountaineering instructor's tip that also helps the pupil wangle favours.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pull strings' looks like using influence; here it is literal, tugging the cord that undoes this kind of knot.
explanation.definitionFit: A knot made so that pulling one end releases it, and spoken it sounds like a caution against losing grip.

clue.text: Text of Animal Bill shortly coming up

indicators.note: in a down clue coming up means read from bottom to top, backwards

parts.note: an otter is an animal

indicators.note: shortly means cut short, losing its last letter

parts.note: Bill is a man's name

explanation.surface: A bill about animals being introduced to Parliament soon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shortly' trims BILL to BIL; 'coming up' reverses OTTER BIL.
explanation.definitionFit: The words of an opera, its written script.

clue.text: Give people in it sense of foreboding

parts.note: to give is to present

indicators.note: the people go inside the two letters of the word it

parts.note: men is a common crossword stand-in for people

explanation.surface: Instilling a feeling of dread in a crowd.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling that something, usually bad, is about to happen.

clue.text: Specify drink in Japan — one is called the same as another

definitions.text: one is called the same as another

parts.note: to name is to specify
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: Ordering rice wine in Tokyo, and meeting someone with your name.
explanation.definitionFit: A person sharing a given name with someone else.

clue.text: Reduce price in spring

explanation.surface: Cutting prices in springtime.
explanation.definitionFit: To deduct from a price, as in taking ten per cent off; a jump or leap into the air.

clue.text: Energetic person may nod off

indicators.note: off means awry, so the letters are disordered

explanation.surface: Even a lively person can doze off.
explanation.definitionFit: A bundle of energy, named after the machine that generates electricity.

clue.text: Touched your hat?

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone touched their hat.
explanation.definitionFit: Past tense of feel, to touch; and the fabric a hat is often made of, as in trilby or fedora.

clue.text: Good-looker? Stanley for one I presume

explanation.surface: A handsome man named Stanley, presumably.
explanation.walkthrough: Stanley found Livingstone in Africa, famously greeting him 'Dr Livingstone, I presume?'
explanation.definitionFit: One who looks thoroughly, a good looker; Stanley went in quest of the missing explorer.

clue.text: Position vague when year is out

indicators.note: out here means put out of order, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A note that something's location is uncertain once the year is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is out' shuffles the eight letters of WHEN YEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: Meaning in some place or other, a position left unspecified.

clue.text: Board lacking leader with legal qualification

indicators.note: the word loses its first letter, its head

parts.note: a table is a board, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: A committee without a chairman, but with a lawyer's credentials.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lacking leader' strips the T from TABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: In law a person who is competent or legally qualified to act is described this way.

clue.text: Vividly descriptive writer employed in the theatre?

explanation.surface: An author with a gift for description who works backstage.
explanation.definitionFit: Figuratively one who sets the scene in words; literally the artist who paints stage backdrops.

clue.text: Method of calculating mathematician's radii, perhaps

parts.note: John Napier, the Scottish mathematician who devised logarithms
the radius is a bone of the forearm, so radii are examples

explanation.surface: A calculation involving a geometer's circles.
explanation.walkthrough: 'radii' suggests circles; it is the forearm bone.
explanation.definitionFit: A set of numbered rods for multiplying, a calculating aid devised in the 1600s.

clue.text: In lines ants are free to range about

indicators.note: set free, the letters of the insects' name are loosed into a new order
turned about, the two letters are read backwards

parts.note: A to Z is the full range, as in an A-Z guide

explanation.surface: Insects allowed to wander wherever they like within boundary lines.
explanation.walkthrough: 'free' scrambles ANTS into STAN; 'about' turns AZ (a range from A to Z) into ZA.
explanation.definitionFit: A group of lines forming a unit of a poem, a verse.

clue.text: One of the easier ways to walk

definitions.text: One of the easier ways to walk

parts.words: One of the easier ways to walk
parts.note: ways means routes rather than manners of walking: a track meant for pedestrians

explanation.surface: A suggestion about gentle forms of exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ways to walk' suggests gaits or styles; it means routes.
explanation.definitionFit: A path for pedestrians, the easy route for walkers compared with roads.

clue.text: Kid sets fire to a tree

parts.note: to kid is to con, to deceive

indicators.note: sets means arranges, so the letters are put in a new order

explanation.surface: A child commits arson on a tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sets' rearranges FIRE into IFER; 'Kid' is a verb, not a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A cone-bearing evergreen such as pine or fir.

clue.text: Sound of day breaking

parts.note: not the noise of anything shattering but the call a farmyard bird gives at first light

explanation.surface: Noise heard as dawn arrives.
explanation.definitionFit: Dawn, marked by a rooster's crowing.

clue.text: Otto, for example, in a temper or tantrum

indicators.note: the letters are found inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: A man named Otto throws a fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to the run tEMPER OR; Otto was the name of several Holy Roman rulers.
explanation.definitionFit: Otto I and others were Holy Roman monarchs, so Otto is an example of such a ruler.

clue.text: Report of female kidnapped in error

indicators.note: report means spoken aloud, so the phrase is heard rather than read

parts.note: a miss, a girl, taken, seized

explanation.surface: A news report of a woman abducted by mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: Wrong, holding a false belief.

clue.text: Dish for which Humpty Dumpty was bound to fall

definitions.text: Dish for which Humpty Dumpty was bound to fall

parts.words: Dish for which Humpty Dumpty was bound to fall
parts.note: Humpty Dumpty, the nursery-rhyme egg, falls and breaks: the first step towards a beaten-egg dish

explanation.surface: A nursery-rhyme character doomed to tumble for the sake of a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fall for' reads as being attracted to; the egg literally falls and cracks.
explanation.definitionFit: A dish of beaten eggs fried in a pan.

clue.text: Launches joint venture, half property, half hotels

indicators.note: half here takes the front four of the eight letters
the second half takes the back three of the six letters

explanation.surface: A business partnership opens, split between real estate and hotels.
explanation.walkthrough: PROP is the first half of property, ELS the second half of hotels.
explanation.definitionFit: Drives forward, as an engine thrusts or a rocket is sent off.

clue.text: Whereby our days are numbered

parts.note: the gloomy phrase about mortality is read literally: the thing that gives each day its date number

explanation.surface: A grim reflection on mortality.
explanation.definitionFit: A table of dates gives each day of the year its number.

clue.text: The tale, say, of the smoker

definitions.text: The tale, say, of the smoker

parts.words: The tale, say, of the smoker
parts.note: tale, say, sounds like tail: the tail end of what a smoker smokes

explanation.surface: A story told by a man with a pipe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tale' suggests a story, but by sound it is tail, the stub end.
explanation.definitionFit: A cigarette butt, the stub left after smoking.

clue.text: Nurse a female in New York

explanation.surface: A nurse looking after a woman in Manhattan.
explanation.definitionFit: A senior hospital nurse holds this title; in American slang a woman is addressed this way.

clue.text: Music maker dwelling in the country quietly

parts.note: a cottage is a small rural house
piano is the musical direction for softly

explanation.surface: Someone making music at their country home without disturbing anyone.
explanation.definitionFit: A small upright keyboard instrument, an instrument that makes music.

clue.text: Mark loses a match.

indicators.note: loses means the letter goes missing from the name

parts.note: Mark Twain, the American author

explanation.surface: A man named Mark is beaten in a game.
explanation.definitionFit: An identical counterpart, one that matches another.

clue.text: Distinctive sound — foreign?

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a characteristic accent comes from abroad.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition is cryptic: E is the abbreviation for English, so what is foreign is 'not E'.
explanation.definitionFit: A tone, as in a note of alarm, is a distinctive sound; jokily, not English means foreign.

clue.text: First Australian without a rating

indicators.note: without means lacking, so those letters are taken away

parts.note: an Aboriginal is a native Australian
AB, able seaman, is a naval rating

explanation.surface: An Australian lacking any score or assessment came first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes AB, an able seaman, the lowest naval rank above ordinary seaman.
explanation.definitionFit: The earliest version is the first, the initial one.

clue.text: Mavis euphoniously described

parts.note: Mavis is not a woman's name but an old word for the song thrush, here pictured as a sweet singer

explanation.surface: A woman named Mavis praised for her pleasant voice.
explanation.walkthrough: Mavis is a dialect name for the song thrush.
explanation.definitionFit: A songbird or singer, a fitting description for a thrush.
